problem: Prior multi-robot LLM/VLM systems (RoCo, CoELA, PARTNR, TeamCraft) do not jointly supervise natural-language inter-robot communication and skill-level action selection in small, vision-conditioned VLMs for decentralized mobile manipulation. There is also no public multimodal dataset for this.
motivation: Robots should run their high-level policies on-device, which requires small (~8B) VLMs. Under partial observability, merely providing a message channel does not tell agents how to divide work, synchronize dependent actions or share fixtures. Off-the-shelf small VLMs almost never coordinate successfully.
key_idea: Synthesize FSM-validated multimodal two-robot demonstrations (leader-follower planning protocol, tool calls, rationale traces, diverse messages) with a strong VLM, then SFT a small VLM to output both messages and skills as tool calls.
insight: Communication access alone is insufficient: for Gemini-3-Flash, success rises from 8%/10% (None/Unguided) to 43% (Minimal) and to 66% in-training / 72% held-out only with the full leader-follower protocol. Rationale supervision improves held-out generalization for both model variants at 30 trajectories per task (Instruct 45→58%, Thinking 50→71%). More demonstrations of the same tasks do not reliably improve held-out success (Instruct 64→55→48→65%).
method: Multi-agent simulator: RoboCasa365 adapted into a two-robot kitchen environment with 53 multi-phase tasks, 60 scene configurations, randomized initial state, spawn positions and leader. Each agent has a private context (own images, tool history, received messages).
Unified tool-call action space: perception, navigation, manipulation, communicate, wait_for_signal and give_space tools serve as high-level actions for both communication and physical acts.

FSM verifier: tracks symbolic task state, validates both agents' tool calls against preconditions and exclusive-resource constraints, and provides the sparse success signal for generation and evaluation.
Coordination rules: leader-follower two-step plan handshake before physical actions, wait-release keyword synchronization, and give_space for exclusive fixture access.

Data generation: Gemini-3-Flash proposes joint trajectories with rationales; the FSM rejects invalid ones and retries with feedback; accepted plans are replayed in simulation to capture images; then split into per-agent next-tool-call examples. Structured Random sampling (low/medium/high communication length, complexity and tool diversity) gives +52% communication diversity.

Training: a single shared VLM policy (Qwen3-VL-8B Instruct or Thinking) fine-tuned with LoRA (r16, α32) for 1 epoch, optionally with rationale in the target; 43 tasks used for training and 10 held out.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking (LoRA fine-tuned); Gemini-3-Flash (frozen) for data generation and baseline
setting.training_data: RoboTalk synthetic dataset: 7,950 FSM-validated trajectories over 53 tasks (43 for SFT, 30-150 trajectories per task); generated by Gemini-3-Flash
setting.observation: Per-agent egocentric RGB images captured at perception-tool calls, plus JSON initial state, tool-call history and received messages
setting.action_space: High-level tool calls (perception, navigation, manipulation, communicate, wait_for_signal, give_space); low-level execution abstracted via FSM
setting.privileged: Abstract JSON initial state given in context and an FSM for symbolic execution and validation (abstract tool execution, not learned low-level control)

numbers.extra: Trained on 43 tasks with rationale targets; success = error-free FSM success within 4x budget
numbers.evidence: Held-out success peaks at 120 trajectories per task, reaching 77%
Full raises success to 66% in-training and 72% held-out

numbers_note: Results in the paper are mostly given in figures; the numbers above are those quoted in the text. Benchmark is the authors' own RoboTalk, not a standard benchmark.
results: Fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on RoboTalk raises success from about 0% to 94% on in-training tasks and 65% on held-out tasks. Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking with rationale traces reaches 77% held-out success, which exceeds Gemini-3-Flash with the full protocol (66% in-training, 72% held-out).
limitations: Evaluation uses abstract tool execution with an FSM instead of learned low-level manipulation or navigation policies, and is simulation-only.
Only two robots, kitchen tasks, and data generated by a single teacher model (Gemini-3-Flash).
Held-out generalization is non-monotonic in data size, and evaluation uses only 10 episodes per task.
